critical_findings.tfidf_hierarchical_v1_6_of_8_pass: TF-IDF hierarchical_v1 protocol: 6/8 modes PASS at 174k (3 text-based at full 173,963: fine_branch_purity 0.906-0.930; 3 citation-based at 52% scale: 0.609-0.685)
critical_findings.r3_source_isolation_reproduces_headline: R3 source isolation (completed 2026-10-10 during resume of run 38048724922) reproduces the accepted 0.906-0.930 fine purity BIT-EXACT on the evaluation-v25 embeddings with the frozen v29 pipeline (full_text 0.93007, regeste_0.5 0.90567, regeste_0.7 0.90889). This is a METRIC-LEVEL reproduction only, NOT a validated branch-recovery claim: the fine partition is over-segmented (365-1316 clusters; fine ARI_branch 0.043-0.047), the coarse ARI_branch is only 0.163-0.258 (weak-to-moderate), and the frozen EVAL_SPEC positive control fails on these source-corrected labels (full_text fine ARI_branch 0.0429 < 0.05). The audited unqualified 'CONFIRMED' label is RETRACTED (audit required_fix F2).
critical_findings.tfidf_ari_branch_micro_pure_macro_unalig: TF-IDF hierarchies at the FINE level are over-segmented (365-1316 clusters) and micro-coherent but macro-unaligned on the 5-class branch axis (fine ARI_branch 0.043-0.047); at the COARSE level the same hierarchy shows weak-to-moderate branch recapture (coarse_ARI_branch 0.2581/0.1747/0.1629), not ~0.04. They remain strongly area-informative (NMI_area 0.555-0.574) - content/thematic clustering, not a branch taxonomy. Granularity correction: the audited report used the fine ARI to characterise the coarse claim (audit required_fix F1).
critical_findings.product_integration_174k_join_scrambled: DATA-INTEGRITY BLOCKER (BLOCKER_PRODUCT_JOIN_ALIGNMENT_V1): product_integration_174k decision_clusters/labels were built by build_production_modes_product_integration_174k.py from the 175440-row product embedding matrix (corpus-jsonl order) positionally truncated to [:173963] and keyed to eval metadata ids with NO row-order verification. Join probe (fractal_map/eval_product_join_alignment_probe_v1.py): diagonal-is-best=0.0% for all 3 text modes, median displacement 1150 rows, 96.8% >1000 rows. id->cluster mapping effectively random (R1 product purity 0.355 vs accepted 0.93; full_text at permutation-chance p=0.23). Rebuild from eval-aligned embeddings required before product promotion. This defect is A cause of the product-vs-source numeric gap and fully explains the id-scrambling, but it is NOT the only cause of the discrepancy: the positive-control failure above is independent of it.
critical_findings.regeste_hybrid_product_modes_never_built: regeste_full_text_hybrid_0.5/0.7 have NO product artifacts under product_integration_174k (R1 errored on missing decision_clusters.json) - product cannot serve the accepted claim for these modes until they are built.

The earlier 'dense 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF citation 0.71-0.74' comparison was an artifact of (a) mismatch of pair sets (dense on 730 pairs, TF-IDF on 1020) and (b) 17% self-pairs (d,d) inflating both by ~0.045 AUC. A full-dimensional citation representation (binary outgoing-citation Jaccard) beats dense on DIRECT citations (0.7735 vs 0.6924) and is an oracle on shared-citation relations (1.000). Product implication: build the citation-heritage view from the citation graph for corpora with resolved citations; use dense embeddings only as a text-only proxy when citation metadata is absent. Dense remains COMPLEMENTARY (cross-lingual view, linear hybrid) and FAILS the jurist gate at all scales. Does not affect the two-mode tradeoff.
critical_findings.section_crosslingual_hierarchy: Section-specific cross-lingual evaluation COMPLETE for all three sections at 1K sample scale. Sachverhalt (facts, n=359) SUPERIOR: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.282, invariance_gap=0.187. Dispositiv (holding, n=538) INTERMEDIATE: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.150, invariance_gap=0.397. Erwaegungen (reasoning, n=510) POOREST: cp_64 cross_lang_same_branch=0.094, invariance_gap=0.452. Center projection improves all (sachverhalt gap 0.304->0.187, erwaegungen 0.538->0.452, dispositiv 0.575->0.397). Legal facts align best cross-lingually; holdings retain some alignment; reasoning is most language-specific. Full corpus density BLOCKED pending section extraction at 174k scale.
critical_findings.linear_hybrids_scale_dependency: Weight sweep at 22-year (144k) reveals OPTIMAL w=0.4 for cited_decisions_tfidf (JP=0.6725, LangDom=0.6539 BOTH PASS) and w=0.3 for outcome_hybrid_0.5 (JP=0.6115, LangDom=0.7477 BOTH PASS). At 19-year optimal was w=0.3 for both. At 15-year linear_hybrid05_concat FAILS (JP=0.473). Scale shifts optimal weight toward denser semantic contribution at larger scale. But BOTH still BELOW TF-IDF baseline (JP=0.784/0.789). Optimal weight shifts toward TF-IDF dominance (w=0.3-0.4 dense / 0.6-0.7 TF-IDF). Citation signals dominate jurist preference; semantic signals add cross-lingual benefit but dilute legal relevance.
critical_findings.two_mode_tradeoff_fundamental: Citation/Outcome (TF-IDF hybrids): LangDom~0.48, JP~0.78, CiteIndep~14%. Semantic Embeddings (center_projected): LangDom~0.83-0.98, JP~0.05-0.43, CiteIndep~37%. Linear Hybrids: LangDom~0.58-0.80, JP~0.61-0.67 (optimal weight), intermediate. NO single representation dominates all three metrics at any scale. TF-IDF citation hybrids = PRIMARY product mode (jurist preference, branch clustering). Dense embeddings = COMPLEMENTARY modes (citation heritage view, cross-lingual view, linear hybrid complement).
critical_findings.dense_embeddings_fail_jurist_gate_all_sc: At 3yr ACCEPTED (19k): JP=0.39-0.42 FAIL. At 15yr (92k): JP=0.288 FAIL. At 19yr (122k): JP=0.37 FAIL. critical_findings.legal_tfidf_bge_corpus_negative: Legal TF-IDF from bge_ corpus (published BGE volumes, 6,243 decisions, 2000-2021) FAILS adversarial suite (6-8/14 PASS vs 14/14 baseline). repair_38779139471_round3.advisory_F2_cluster_label_environment_se: FIXED for the label-ordering defect it diagnosed. RESTATED BY RUN 38789874982: the repair's *environment-independence* evidence was produced by varying PYTHONHASHSEED on the generating host, where the absolute cache path is constant by construction, so it did not establish the property being claimed. The label determinism itself is real (0 of 37 label terms across all 8 clusters are absent from their cluster; stable under 1e-16 last-bit noise). Artifact identity is now established by v51_delivery.repair_38789874982_round4 instead. Original finding, preserved: FIXED. Cause measured rather than assumed: six replays of the claim query produced three different file sha256 values locally (three with default hash randomisation, three with PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/2); exactly five fields vary between replays and all five are wall-clock timings, so a raw file hash can never match across runs. The data difference the auditor saw came from build_map's terms[np.argsort(-mean)[:5]] over the whole 5000-term vocabulary: for clusters of 1-5 decisions only a few terms have a non-zero mean, so the 4th/5th label slots came from thousands of exactly tied zero-mean terms. Repair: product/query/qmap.py::label_terms is now the single ranking for both the initial fit and the recompute-on-merge path, admits only mean > 0 and orders by (-round(mean, 9), term). Effect measured on the claim bundle: no label names an absent term any more (the one-decision cluster C7 read 'ptt, betriebe, unterstehen, zugefagt, privatrecht' where three of those five terms occur in no member; it now reads 'ptt, betriebe, benutzern, betrieben, beurteilt'), and x/y/is_outlier/citation/source_url/rank/score are byte-identical on 154/154 rows with identical per-cluster membership sets.
repair_38779139471_round3.advisory_F3_citation_view_empty_no_follo: FIXED. Relations were produced only by find_citations string matching over decision bodies, which are empty for 30 of 154 unhydrated citation shells, so the map's 'reveal relations on selection' affordance (QUERY_MAP_MVP 7) was empty for the whole query. The OpenCaseLaw /citations channel already returns typed edges and the accepted adapter records each on the candidate row's provenance_events (seed_decision_id, direction, confidence, mention_count), but to_product_bundle emits relations: [] and frontier/** is outside product write scope. Repair: product/query/pipeline.py::typed_citation_relations rebuilds each edge with one reading direction (source cites target), emits it only when both endpoints are on the map, de-duplicates; _merge_relations prefers typed edges and de-duplicates per decision pair; progressive.py re-derives them after expansion; query.html states the direction ('a cite X' / 'a cite par X') with the upstream confidence.
